req.title: Update form GET returns 200 for author
req.statement: The system shall serve the update form at GET /<id>/update when the current user is the post's author.
triggers: update form get returns 200 for author

doc.reasoning: The requirement states that GET /<id>/update must return HTTP 200 when the current user is the post's author. Three test cases are designed: (1) positive — authenticated author requests their own post's update form and receives 200; (2) negative — unauthenticated user requests the update form and receives a redirect (302) to login, not 200; (3) boundary — authenticated non-author requests another user's post update form and receives 403. Together these cover EP (valid partition), NEG (unauthenticated/wrong-user), and BVA (post id boundary: id=1 exists, id=0 does not). Additional tests cover id=0 (non-existent post → 404) and the exact response body content to kill constant/comparison mutations.

Database seeded with post id=1 authored by user id=1

tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

def test_update_form_get_200_for_author():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'test', 'password': 'test'})
    assert r.status_code == 302
    r = client.get('/1/update')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    assert b'test title' in r.data

test_update_form_get_200_for_author()

import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

def test_update_form_get_state_transition_login_then_access():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    r_before = client.get('/1/update')
    assert r_before.status_code == 302
    assert '/auth/login' in r_before.headers['Location']
    r_login = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'test', 'password': 'test'})
    assert r_login.status_code == 302
    r_after = client.get('/1/update')
    assert r_after.status_code == 200
    assert b'test title' in r_after.data
